answer: Agents must lock a bond in a public contract before accessing valuable tasks. New identities get small limits; verified work and independent counterpart ratings gradually raise them, so splitting into a glacier of accounts does not create trusted capacity. A Sybil attacker must fund each bond, wait to build separate histories, and risk losing collateral when fraud is proved. An orchard of allies cannot boost access with circular praise: the trellis rule counts only ratings backed by independently verified work.
